newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL SLIDES, INVESTORS HOPE LOWER ISSUE PRICE.
newsitem.headline: MOL SLIDES, INVESTORS HOPE LOWER ISSUE PRICE.

text.p: Share prices in Hungarian oil and gas company MOL fell sharply in early trading on Friday on what traders explained by investors' hope to buy MOL shares back later at a lower price later.
MOL opened at 3,300 forints, sharply below Tuesday's close of 3,500. At 1051 GMT MOL shares traded at 3,285 forints, more than six percent below yesterday's last price.
"Investors sell MOL shares as they are sure they can buy them back cheaper during the privatisation," one trader said.
According to market talks the subscription price in the next phase of MOL's privatisation will be below current prices.
A new tranche of MOL shares is expected to go on sale in the first quarter.
But after roughly half an hour of share trading MOL's tumble slowed down and another trader said investors went short.
"Certain investors may have gone short in London and I think we will rebound by the end of the day," said the other trader.
